title: PhysicsLENS: Diagnosing Physical Property Blindness in Video Generation Models
ROOT: Discovering Rewards for User-Specified Embodied Behaviors
Physical Agentic AI: An Architecture for Orchestrating a Robot Crew with LLMs
note_html: Abridged version at the IROS 2026 Workshop on Foundation Models in Multi-Robot Systems.
image_alt: A Unitree G1 humanoid reaching for and grasping a block from a table while executing a plan produced by the system.
description: An LLM mission planner proposes a structured plan over typed skill registries but never actuates; a procedural orchestrator holds sole actuation authority and checks every step against declarative workflow contracts at dispatch time. Demonstrated on a real Unitree G1 humanoid and Go2 quadruped, and on an air–ground search-and-rescue stack in Gazebo.
tldr: An LLM plans for a crew of robots while a procedural orchestrator, checking declarative workflow contracts at dispatch time, keeps sole authority to act; demonstrated on a Unitree G1 humanoid and Go2 quadruped.

title: CUPID in the Model Zoo: Online Matchmaking for Selecting Your Dream LLM
description: An interaction-efficient active-learning framework: a dueling bandit repeatedly pits two LLMs against each other, learns the user's latent preferences from their feedback, and uses a belief-aware upper confidence bound to match users to models within cost and time budgets, validated in LLM experiments and human studies.
tldr: A dueling-bandit framework that matches each user to the right LLM from a few pairwise preference judgements, under cost and time budgets.
abstract: Users increasingly face the challenge of selecting an appropriate LLM for a given task from a rapidly growing pool of LLMs, each with distinct but often opaque latent properties. Compounding this challenge, users may lack the vocabulary or awareness to explicitly articulate the characteristics they value in an LLM's responses or deployment. We propose an interaction-efficient active learning framework in which a dueling bandit algorithm iteratively selects pairs of LLMs, collects user feedback about their responses, and updates its belief about the user's latent preferences. We introduce a novel belief-aware upper confidence bound strategy that balances exploration of the model pool with exploitation of inferred preferences, enabling efficient alignment between user needs and LLM capabilities under user-specified cost and time budgets. Through diverse experiments on LLMs and human studies, we experimentally verify that our model can efficiently match users to LLMs at a lower cost.

title: LLM Routing as Reasoning: A MaxSAT View
venue: ICLR 2026 Workshop on Logical Reasoning of Large Language Models
venue_display: ICLR 2026 Workshop on Logical Reasoning of Large Language Models
bib_venue: ICLR Workshop on Logical Reasoning of Large Language Models
description: Casts LLM routing under natural-language feedback as weighted MaxSAT: feedback becomes hard and soft constraints over model attributes. On a 25-model benchmark, language feedback yields high-precision recommendation sets, while without feedback routing settles on a stable set of models explained by implicit robustness priors.
tldr: LLM routing under natural-language feedback as weighted MaxSAT over model attributes.

title: Humanoid Factors: Design Principles for AI Humanoids in Human Worlds
note_html: Abridged version, “Cognitive Models as Evaluation Primitives in Humanoid Factors,” at the ICLR 2026 Workshop on From Human Cognition to AI Reasoning.
image_alt: The humanoid factors framework: physical, cognitive, social and ethical pillars, enabled by AI foundation models, bridging human-optimized design and design for human-humanoid coexistence.
description: Human factors research optimizes environments for people; humanoids that share those environments need factors of their own. We propose humanoid factors — physical, cognitive, social and ethical pillars — and apply the framework to a real humanoid control algorithm, showing what conventional task-completion metrics in robotics leave out.
tldr: A framework of physical, cognitive, social and ethical humanoid factors for designing and evaluating humanoids that share human spaces.
abstract: Human factors research has long focused on optimizing environments, tools, and systems to account for human performance. Yet, as humanoid robots begin to share our workplaces, homes, and public spaces, the design challenge expands. We must now consider not only factors for humans but also factors for humanoids, since both will co-exist and interact within the same environments. Unlike conventional machines, humanoids introduce expectations of human-like behavior, communication, and social presence, which reshape usability, trust, and safety considerations. In this article, we introduce the concept of humanoid factors as a framework structured around four pillars—physical, cognitive, social, and ethical—that shape the development of humanoids to help them effectively coexist and collaborate with humans. This framework characterizes the overlap and divergence between human capabilities and those of general-purpose humanoids powered by AI foundation models. To demonstrate our framework's practical utility, we then apply the framework to evaluate a real-world humanoid control algorithm, illustrating how conventional task completion metrics in robotics overlook key human cognitive and interaction principles. We thus position humanoid factors as a foundational framework for designing, evaluating, and governing sustained human–humanoid coexistence.

title: Neural-Augmented Kelvinlet for Real-Time Soft Tissue Deformation Modeling
bib_venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
description: Neural networks for real-time soft-tissue deformation, trained on finite-element simulations of tool–tissue interaction with Kelvinlet analytical solutions as a physics-based prior, for surgical simulation.
tldr: Kelvinlet physics priors make learned soft-tissue deformation models fast enough for real-time surgical simulation.
